open_questions.question: Which statistics and groupings the traces view offers. Settled in slice 'traces-you-can-browse' (operator, 2026-11-02, then confirmed in the mock): cost, duration and errors first; tokens, model and tool calls and waiting time second; grouping switchable between agent, model, task, conversation, kind and day; the view lives inside Activity, with the Hub's own traces behind a quieter 'Hub internals' choice.
What the woven view weaves. Operator 2026-11-02: the agents working one task or build, one lane per agent, with hand-off links (the recommendation).

problem:
Checkpoints are generated well (75 on the operator's Hub on 2026-11-02, 73 passed their probe), but the only screen for them is a modal limited to one conversation, reached from an overflow menu. 75 checkpoints are spread across 74 conversations, so it rarely shows more than one, and a conversation that was carried over from a checkpoint shows none. Bodies are raw markdown, labels are internal vocabulary, and nothing tells one checkpoint from another at a glance. A checkpoint can only be used through the one-time cut-over offer, which keeps the same agent and archives the old conversation.

Traces open one run at a time, from a faint per-turn link or a task story row. The only list is ten rows inside Project Settings, filtered by kind only. There is no trace of a whole conversation, no agent or time filter, no grouping, and no statistics.

in_scope: Traces: a project-level traces view with filters, grouping and statistics, as a view inside Activity.
Traces: a trace of a whole conversation, choosing which runs and from when.
Traces: a woven view of the agents working one task or build, one lane per agent on a shared time axis, with the hand-offs between them drawn as links.

Checkpoints: a project-level view and links from where work happens; each checkpoint's trigger, agent, conversation and runs shown; a readable body; a title and summary written by the checkpoint itself, and filled once for existing checkpoints.
Checkpoints: starting a new conversation from any checkpoint, older ones included, with any agent.
non_goals: A separate, ongoing distillation or manager run over checkpoints. The checkpoint generation is already that run; it is asked for a title and summary instead (operator, 2026-11-02).
Trace retention, OTLP export, download and clearing; they stay in Project Settings.
What the Hub records as spans.

slices.done: From Activity → Traces the operator narrows to one agent's runs over a chosen time range, groups them by another dimension, and sees statistics that change with the filter.
slices.intent: Traces get a view of their own inside Activity, rather than a list in Settings, where the operator filters by agent, conversation, task, run, kind and time range, groups them in different ways, and reads statistics over what is shown.
slices.title: A traces view with filters, grouping and stats

slices.done: Opening a conversation's trace shows all its runs on one timeline, and narrowing to a run range or start time redraws it.
slices.intent: From a conversation the operator opens one trace covering its runs, choosing which runs and from when, instead of one run at a time.
slices.title: A trace of a whole conversation

slices.done: For a build with several agents, the woven view shows each agent's runs in its own lane in the order they happened, and the hand-off that started each run is drawn from the lane it came from.
slices.intent: For one task or build, the operator sees the agents who worked it as lanes on a shared time axis, each run a block that opens its trace, with the hand-offs between agents (an assignment or message that started a run, a completion, a review, a send-back) drawn as links between lanes.
slices.title: Woven traces

slices.done: On the operator's Hub, the checkpoints view lists all checkpoints across agents and conversations, filterable by agent and trigger, and every checkpoint, old and new, shows a title and summary.
slices.intent: The operator opens one place and sees every checkpoint in the project. Each is identifiable at a glance by its title, agent, trigger and date, and opens as readable text with the runs it covers. A carried-over conversation shows the checkpoint it started from.
slices.title: Every checkpoint, findable and readable

slices.done: Starting from a checkpoint that was already carried over, with a different agent than the one that produced it, opens a new conversation for that agent whose first input is that checkpoint, and the original conversation is not archived.
slices.intent: The operator picks any checkpoint, including an older or already carried-over one, chooses any agent, and a new conversation for that agent starts from it, leaving the original conversation as it was.
slices.title: Start a conversation from any checkpoint

summary: Rework the checkpoint and trace screens so they serve how AgentWeave is used: picking up where an agent left off (checkpoints), and debugging a run or auditing a task or build (traces). Each gets a project-level view and links from the screens where the work happens. Traces are built first (operator, 2026-11-02). Each slice is mocked interactively once it is specified, then approved and built against that mock.
title: Checkpoints and traces you can find and use
